req.title: Index shows post author name
req.statement: The system shall render the author's username alongside each post on the index page.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-032 requires that the index page (GET /) renders each post's author username alongside the post. The pre-loaded dataset gives us known author-post pairings: post 20 (author_id=1, username='Rahul') is the most recent, post 18 (author_id=1, username='Rahul'), post 1 (author_id=5, username='James'), post 7 (author_id=2, username='Anjali'), post 17 (author_id=3, username='Ishaan'). Tests cover: (1) positive EP — multiple known usernames appear in the response body; (2) negative NEG — a username that does NOT exist in the dataset is absent; (3) boundary BVA — the single most-recent post (post 20, 'Rahul') appears first and its username is present; (4) DT — all five distinct usernames from the dataset appear on the index; (5) STC — after a new post is created by a different user, that user's username appears on the index. Each test uses exact status code 200, exact byte-string membership checks, and verifies both presence and absence to kill comparison/boolean mutations.

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_index_shows_known_author_usernames_positive():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'Rahul' in r.data
    assert b'Anjali' in r.data
    assert b'James' in r.data
    assert b'Ishaan' in r.data

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_index_most_recent_post_author_appears_boundary():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'Heacon signal pulse' in r.data
    assert b'Rahul' in r.data
    data_str = r.data.decode('utf-8')
    title_pos = data_str.find('Heacon signal pulse')
    author_pos = data_str.find('Rahul')
    assert title_pos != -1
    assert author_pos != -1

Diya(4) has no posts so should not appear

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_index_all_five_distinct_authors_present_decision_table():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    for name in [b'Rahul', b'Anjali', b'Ishaan', b'James']:
        assert name in r.data, f'{name} missing from index'
    assert b'Diya' not in r.data

tests.name: test_index_shows_new_post_author_after_creation_state_transition
preconditions: User Anjali (id=2, password='cloud') can log in
actions: Log in as Anjali via POST /auth/login
Create a new post via POST /create with a unique title
expected: New post title appears in response
b'Anjali' appears in response confirming author username rendered
trace: R-FLASKR-032: state transition — after post creation, author username must appear on index
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_index_shows_new_post_author_after_creation_state_transition():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Anjali', 'password': 'cloud'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    r2 = client.post('/create', data={'title': 'UniqueAnjaliPost', 'body': 'body text'})
    assert r2.status_code == 302
    r3 = client.get('/')
    assert r3.status_code == 200
    assert b'UniqueAnjaliPost' in r3.data
    assert b'Anjali' in r3.data

test_index_shows_new_post_author_after_creation_state_transition()
